question: My partner and I separated because our relationship broke down. Do I report myself as separated to CRA after just one month apart?
generated_answer:
The CRA considers you separated if you and your spouse or common-law partner are living apart for at least 90 days or more due to a breakdown in your relationship. If you have been apart for less than 90 days, you are not considered separated for tax purposes.

If you have been apart for 90 days or more, you should report yourself as separated to the CRA. You can do this by filing a change of address form with the CRA and by updating your marital status on your tax return.

It's important to note that even if you are separated, you may still be considered common-law for tax purposes if you have lived together for 12 consecutive months in a relationship that is like a marriage. If this is the case, you will need to continue to file your taxes as common-law until you have been apart for 12 months.

If you are unsure about your situation, it's best to contact the CRA directly for guidance.

Here is a link to the CRA's page on Separation and Divorce: [https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/separation-divorce.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/separation-divorce.html) 

And here is a link to the CRA's page on Filing a Change of Address: [https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/changes-addresses/changing-your-address.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/changes-addresses/changing-your-address.html) 

Remember to also update your address with any other government agencies or private organizations that may need to know your current address.
